rows.text: The February 2011 version of the Assembly's Speakers list gives the same spans as the November 2011 version (Nopele Malupo 1987 - 1989, Nopele Fusitu'a 1990 - 1998, Nopele Veikune 1999 - 2001; 2005 - 2006, Nopele Tu'ivakano 2002 - 2004, Nopele Tu'ilakepa 2008 - 2010) except 'Nopele Havea Tu'iha'angana 2006 - 2007'. Its Tongan introduction says that the King appoints the Speaker (Sea) from the nobles under clause 61 of the Constitution and section ('Kupu') 15 of the Legislative Assembly Act, and that 16 people had been appointed Speaker since 1875.
rows.locator: Tongan introduction ('Mafai', 'Hisitolia'); the 'More Articles...' list on page 1
rows.uncertainty: Retrospective list; attested_on is the capture date. Only the first eight entries (1875-1958) carry created and updated stamps of 10 December 2010; the later entries, including Tu'iha'angana's, are in the undated 'More Articles...' list. Recorded to show that the Assembly's own list changed Tu'iha'angana's final year between February and November 2011. The clause 61 and section 15 description is procedure only. Not a boundary.

bounded_scope: Speaker observations for CLAUDE-C01-24 only (role to_speaker on the to_legislative_assembly observation). Royal appointment, the Assembly's election or recommendation of its Speaker, the oath, a resignation, a revocation, an acting or interim Speaker and a Deputy Speaker presiding stay separate rows; holder observations are decided in the packet, not by any row.
